title: Germany Fails to Win Non-Permanent UN Security Council Seat, Loses to Austria and Portugal
detail: In a secret-ballot vote in the UN General Assembly on June 2–3, Germany lost its bid for one of two non-permanent Security Council seats allocated to the 'Western Europe and Others' group for the 2027–2028 term. Portugal and Austria won with 134 and 131 votes respectively, while Germany's bid — led by Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul — received only 104 votes, falling well short of the two-thirds majority required. It marks a rare diplomatic setback for Berlin, which has held the seat multiple times in past decades. Analysts pointed to several factors: Germany's steadfast diplomatic and military support for Israel amid the ongoing Middle East conflict may have cost votes among African, Asian and Latin American delegations; Austria's constitutionally mandated military neutrality and non-NATO status appealed to non-aligned states; and Austria had campaigned for the seat years earlier than Germany, building a diplomatic head start. Wadephul acknowledged that 'Germany must always assume a special responsibility for Israel,' conceding this likely factored into the vote. The loss fuels domestic criticism of the Merz government's foreign policy standing at a time when Chancellor Merz is already under pressure over sliding approval ratings.

media.caption: Germany lost its UN Security Council bid to Austria and Portugal
